narrative.overview:
Inkroom is a desk with a sheet of paper and one pen of indigo ink. A tutor on a PC and a student on an iPad draw on the same sheet in real time, and everything around the sheet steps back so the drawing stays in front. The paper is cool, never cream. Instruments float above the sheet as small frosted islands. Colour is mostly absent: the one indigo of the brand's pen nib marks what is active, chosen or focused, and nothing else.

This is an Operate surface: people come to teach and learn, not to admire the interface. Ambition shows as precision and restraint. Controls are generous targets for a finger or a stylus (40px tools, 44px fields on touch), labels are short Polish words in sentence case, and the layout changes its shape to fit the device: a wide bar on a PC, a compact bar on a smaller window, a rail down the left edge on a tablet held upright.

Dark mode is a night desk, not an inverted page. The board turns a deep blue-black, default black ink is painted in the light violet of the logo, white ink is painted black, and the indigo lifts to a lighter tone so it still reads as the same pen.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (nib indigo) on a cool grey-white paper; everything else is neutral.
Floating, frosted islands over a full-bleed drawing canvas.
Two radii only: 12px for controls, 18px for containers and islands.
One typeface (Inter) in three working weights; monospace only for formulas.
Touch-first sizing, since the main student device is a tablet with a stylus.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Indigo means "this is on, chosen, or focused". If an element is not in one of those states, it is not indigo. Primary actions are filled with Ink Text, not with indigo.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds stay cool and nearly white (or blue-black at night). No cream, beige or warm tints anywhere.

rules.name: The Swap, Don't Invert Rule
rules.body: In dark mode stored black ink is painted light violet (`nib-indigo-night`) and stored white is painted black. Every other ink colour stays as drawn. Board previews are shown as a dark sheet with light ink, never as a white rectangle.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and headings are written as sentences. No uppercase, no letter-spacing on small labels, no eyebrow above a heading.

rules.name: The Mono Means Maths Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for formulas and the digits of the maths tools. Dates, sizes and the zoom level use Inter with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Float Over Ink Rule
rules.body: Only things above the drawing float (islands, popovers, dialogs). Content on a page (tiles, forms) is flat and bordered, and lifts only in response to the pointer.

dos: **Do** keep indigo for active, selected and focused states only (The One Ink Rule).
**Do** use 12px corners for controls and 18px for containers, and nothing in between.
**Do** make every tool and button at least 40px, and fields and touch pills 44px.
**Do** write labels in sentence-case Polish, as short as the action ("Utwórz tablicę", "Wyloguj", "Zmień hasło").
**Do** float tools over the canvas as frosted islands with the single Island shadow.
**Do** show dates, sizes and zoom in Inter with tabular figures.
**Do** design both themes together: Night Desk, Night Sheet and the lighter indigo for dark mode.
**Do** give a dead end a way out (the missing-board page links back home).
**Do** keep motion under 220ms, opacity and scale only, and switch it off for reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use tracked uppercase labels or eyebrows above headings.
**Don't** use monospace for anything except formulas and maths digits.
**Don't** fill large areas or primary buttons with indigo.
**Don't** add warm, cream or beige backgrounds, gradients, or gradient text.
**Don't** put a coloured bar down one side of a card; use the full Hairline border or the indigo tint.
**Don't** add a second, heavier shadow or hard offset shadows.
**Don't** let islands overlap each other or the canvas tools on any screen from 375px up.
**Don't** show a light, white board preview on the dark theme.
**Don't** animate anything on the drawing canvas or anything that delays a stroke or a tool switch.
